_readme: Kavyas the project intends to hold that the importer has no source for --
the Madhva-lineage mahakavyas above all. tools/build_kavya_tracker.py folds
this together with what is actually on disk and what the Kavya corpus
carries, and writes admin/config/kavya-status.json and dge/KAVYA_TRACKER.md.
`dictated` is what was said, kept verbatim. `id`/`name_iast` is the reading.
`confidence` is about the READING, not about whether the work exists: where
it is not high, the entry says what else it could be and is not to be acted
on until the project lead confirms. This is the same convention PENDING.md's
grantha acquisition list uses, and for the same reason -- a garbled title
sends someone hunting for a text that was never named.
`expected_verses` is null wherever nobody has counted. The dictated estimate
was 'five hundred, six hundred, two thousand slokas each', which is a range,
not a figure, and is recorded as `dictated_scale` rather than guessed into a
number the tracker would then report as fact.

works.author: Sri Narayana Panditacharya
works.note: 16 sargas of mula are published. Its tikas -- Bhavaprakashika and others named in the tradition -- are not in the repo; the exact set is for the project lead to name.

works.author: Sri Narayanacharya
works.note: 10 sargas of mula are published, every shloka carrying an empty commentaries block. This is the case the project lead raised: text yes, commentary not yet.

works.author: Sri Vadiraja Tirtha
works.note: Vadiraja's mahakavya on Krishna. Neither mula nor tika in the repo.

works.author: unconfirmed
works.note: NOT RESOLVED. Heard as 'kushaharana' in a spoken list of Madhva-lineage kavyas. Kusha-harana is not a title this session could confirm against any source. Candidates worth putting to the project lead: a Kusha-lava episode kavya, or a mis-hearing of another Vijaya title in the same breath. Deliberately not guessed into a Devanagari title, because a wrong one sends someone hunting for a text that does not exist.
